Hana (Sales): @Diego urgent — Prospect Beta's POC demo failing. SSE starts then client crashes with `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input`. Repro on Chrome mobile and via their corp proxy.

Diego (SE): Do you have the raw fragments and which SDK (cdn) they're using?

Hana (Sales): Yuna pasted this from network tab (redacted):
```
data: {\"id\":\"b-900\",\"frag\":\"{\\\"reply\\\":\\\"Buen\"}

```
next event:
```
data: {\"id\":\"b-900\",\"frag\":\"os dias\\\"}\n
```
They call `JSON.parse(event.data)` per SSE message. SDK: `@redwood/stream-js@1.1.0` from CDN.

Yuna (Client Eng): Also saw split of multibyte sequences — one fragment ends mid-UTF8 char. Their proxy injects `content-encoding: gzip`.

Diego (SE): Likely causes: proxy/edge gzip or buffering that re-chunks the event stream; older SDK incremental decoder not preserving incomplete bytes. Quick triage: 1) curl -N -v to capture raw stream boundaries, 2) check headers for `content-encoding` and `content-type: text/event-stream`, 3) try forcing websocket fallback in SDK for the demo.

Hana (Sales): Customer worried about firewall/SSO for websocket. Also asked if this is a deal blocker or will affect pricing.

Diego (SE): Websockets use wss:// over 443 — usually allowed through corporate firewalls and uses the same token-based auth. No pricing difference; it's just transport. For Dedicated/on-prem we may need port config but hosted should be fine. I'll draft a short security blurb.

Yuna (Client Eng): Quick repro: I mirrored their proxy locally with gzip enabled and reproduced the split fragments. Turning gzip off on the streaming route stops the problem.

Diego (SE): Workarounds (ranked):
- Fastest for demo: websocket fallback (`new RedwoodClient({ transport: 'websocket', token })`)
- If they can't use ws: client-side reassembly keyed by id and only JSON.parse when payload completes (brace-count or id markers)
- Medium: ask infra to disable gzip / `proxy_buffering off` for the streaming route
- Long: upgrade to `@redwood/stream-js@1.4.x` which has incremental UTF-8 buffering fixes

Yuna (Client Eng): I'll send a tiny buffer snippet to them. Also asked for HAR + `curl -N` output which I'll attach.

Hana (Sales): Please also include the security blurb for their infra/security team. They need an answer today for demo planning.

Diego (SE): Draft blurb (short): "Websocket (wss) connections use TLS on port 443 and authenticate via the same bearer tokens as SSE. Connection and request traces are logged in our audit pipeline; session joins/leaves appear in the same console. For Dedicated deployments, confirm allowed outbound/inbound ports with ops; for Hosted no additional firewall rules are typically needed." Feel free to copy/paste.

infra-bot: Deployed patch stream-proxy-telemetry v2027.08.15 by @diego — includes updated docs on websocket fallback and added tests for incremental UTF-8 handling.

Yuna (Client Eng): Attached har + curl output in the DM to Hana. They tested websocket fallback and demo passed.

Hana (Sales): Great — customer chose websocket fallback for the live walkthrough. Action items: Diego to send security blurb in email, Yuna to share buffer snippet in case infra wants to patch, Hana to update deal notes. Closing if no regressions after demo. :thumbsup:
